title: Perfect love casts out fear; doubt of justification cannot coexist with perfect charity
source_text: XV. Praeterea, non potest non esse defectus vituperabilis id quod perfecta charitas expellit, quodque cum ea consistere non potest. Sed cum incertitudine de justificatione & gratia propria perfecta charitas non potest consistere. Nam, ut docet Joannes, Perfecta charitas foras mittit timorem; quoniam timor poenam habet: qui autem timet non est perfectus in charitate. 1 Joan. 4. Adeoque qui de Dei erga se amore & favore dubitat, necessario timet; nec potest non timere, timore illo qui poenam secum habet. Adeoque perfecta charitas compati non potest secum ejusmodi dubitationem.
pass_a_gloss: Besides, that cannot fail to be a blameworthy defect which perfect charity casts out and which cannot stand with it. But perfect charity cannot stand with uncertainty concerning justification and one’s own grace. For as John teaches, perfect charity casts out fear, because fear has punishment; and he who fears is not perfected in charity (1 John 4). And so whoever doubts God’s love and favor toward himself necessarily fears, and cannot but fear with that fear which has punishment with it. And therefore perfect charity cannot suffer such doubt with itself.
pass_b_english: Perfect love drives out punitive fear; lingering doubt of grace cannot coexist with it.
John’s teaching makes uncertainty about one’s justification a defect charity excludes.
